Observable Resolve Behavior

withCoreObservableBehavior is a resolve behavior that normalizes observable-based state inputs by subscribing to an observable source and extracting a single emitted value for downstream pipeline processing.

This behavior operates exclusively in the Resolve stage. It affects how an incoming value is resolved, never when it enters the pipeline or how it is later processed. No state mutation, derivation, or policy logic occurs as part of observable resolution.

State updates may be submitted through the FeatureCell APIs replaceState and mergeState. Each API admits a distinct category of input, but all inputs converge on the same Resolve stage for classification and normalization before downstream processing.

withCoreObservableBehavior operates exclusively in the Resolve stage, executing after interceptors and before operators. It participates only when an Observable<T> input is supplied to a state update API.

This behavior resolves observable-based inputs by extracting a single emitted value and forwarding it as a normalized upstream value for downstream pipeline processing. Observable errors are normalized and propagated as pipeline errors.

Note
Recommended to use a merge behavior or it is pointless because the state will be replaced with each new emission. For example, if you want to append to an array, use
  • withArrayAppendMergeBehavior
  • withArrayPushMergeBehavior
Diagrams
Configuration

withCoreObservableBehavior requires no explicit configuration parameters. It participates automatically when a state update is supplied with an Observable<T> input via replaceState or mergeState.

The behavior is installed by default as part of the Resolve stage and activates conditionally based on the resolved input type. When an observable input is detected, the behavior subscribes during pipeline execution and resolves a single emitted value for downstream processing.

Subscription lifetime is bound to the FeatureCell lifecycle. Active subscriptions are terminated automatically on reset or destruction, ensuring that observable resolution does not outlive the pipeline execution that initiated it.

Examples

withCoreFromStreamBehavior enables observable streams to be connected directly to a FeatureCell via the fromStream() API. This method establishes a subscription that continuously injects emitted values into the pipeline as state updates.

In the examples below, a FeatureCell is initialized normally. After initialization, an observable stream is attached using fromStream(). Each emitted value is converted into a state update and forwarded through the Resolve stage before being finalized by the State stage.

Example 1: Stream Values into a FeatureCell

{{`@FeatureCell`}}<Employee[]>{{`('employees')
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class EmployeeService {
  private readonly vault = injectVault`}}<Employee[]>{{`(EmployeeService);

  constructor(private readonly http: HttpClient) {
    this.vault.initialize();

    // Observable defined locally in the cell
    const employees$ = of([
      { id: 1, name: 'Alice' },
      { id: 2, name: 'Bob' }
    ]);

    // Submit an observable-based state update
    this.vault.replaceState(employees$);
  }
}`}}
 
{{`import { from } from 'rxjs';

export const employeeCell = FeatureCell`}}<Employee[]>{{`(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [],
  }
);

employeeCell.initialize();

// Observable defined locally in the module
const employees$ = of([
  { id: 1, name: 'Alice' },
  { id: 2, name: 'Bob' }
]);

// Submit an observable-based state update
employeeCell.replaceState(employees$);`}}
